candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record presents findings (elevated CEA and CA19-9, diffuse pancreatic enlargement with delayed enhancement and capsule-like rim, diffuse FDG uptake in pancreas and hypermetabolic lymph nodes, stenosis of lower bile duct and diffuse narrowing of main pancreatic duct) that are more consistent with pancreatic adenocarcinoma than autoimmune pancreatitis. While some features like diffuse enlargement can be seen in both, the tumor markers and FDG avidity strongly point away from autoimmune pancreatitis as the most likely diagnosis.

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is the most common and implied subtype of pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and the clinical findings (jaundice, abdominal pain, elevated bilirubin, hepatobiliary enzymes, HbA1c 7.2%, elevated CEA and CA19-9, diffuse pancreatic enlargement with delayed enhancement and capsule-like rim, intrahepatic bile-duct dilation, diffuse FDG uptake in pancreas and hypermetabolic lymph nodes, stenosis of lower bile duct and diffuse narrowing of main pancreatic duct) are highly suggestive of this diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma vs Pancreatic adenocarcinoma

candidate_relations.reason: Pancreatic Cancer is a broader category that includes pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The reference diagnosis specifies the adenocarcinoma subtype, which is supported by the clinical findings.
